Good catch — confirmed and fixed in f69b66f.

It reproduces on the RABA fixture. Both of these instants are Friday 2025-06-13 in `America/Los_Angeles`, and only the second has rolled over to the 14th in UTC:

```
13:00 local (2025-06-13T20:00Z) -> 15 stops
22:00 local (2025-06-14T05:00Z) -> 12 stops
```

The two dates have genuinely different service: `20250613` has 5 active service IDs, `20250614` has 4. So a UTC-hosted instance serving a Pacific agency answered against the wrong service date for roughly seven hours every evening.

Loading the agency location before resolving the parameter fixes both routes to the fallback. Delegating the empty parameter to `ParseTimeParameter` — which already returns the current time in the location it is given — also drops a branch.

`TestStopsForLocationUsesAgencyDateForCurrentTime` covers the absent and malformed cases separately, since they reach the fallback by different paths; each was mutation-verified against its own path.

@aaronbrethorst worth noting this half is a pre-existing defect on the no-`time` path rather than part of #1350, and it changes the service date every request without a `time` param resolves to. I fixed it here because the helper this PR introduces would otherwise read the parameter in one timezone and its own fallback in another, which the doc comment would have been lying about. Happy to split it into its own issue and PR if you'd rather keep #1350 to the format parsing — and either way it may deserve a card entry, since the same fallback pattern likely appears on other endpoints.

FYI (non-blocking, no code change needed): did a full spec-conformance pass on this while reviewing and updated the wiki with what we found — no action needed here.

- Documented the malformed-`time` fallback (falls back to current time rather than erroring), which matched legacy but wasn't written down: [stops-for-location § Extensions, 4a](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/stops-for-location#extensions).
- Traced legacy's actual timezone handling for the current-time fallback: Java resolves it from the server JVM's own default timezone (a single process-wide setting), never per-agency. Your fix — resolving it against the queried agency's timezone instead — is a deliberate improvement over that, not a literal port of Java's mechanism, so it's now written up as its own decision rather than left implied: [stops-for-location § Implementation Decisions](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/stops-for-location#implementation-decisions).
- Flagged the `agencies[0]` stand-in this (and `trips-for-location`) uses for "the queried agency" as a single-feed-limitation deviation, tracked in the [Multi-Agency-Static-Feeds-Stop-Consolidation §10 table](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/Multi-Agency-Static-Feeds-Stop-Consolidation#10-deviations-from-legacy-due-to-the-single-feed-limitation) to revisit once multi-feed support lands.

Nice catch on the pre-existing UTC-fallback bug, and thanks for the reproduction detail in your commit message — made this easy to verify.

`queryTimeForStops` only uses the agency timezone when a non-empty `time` param is provided. For an absent or malformed `time`, it falls back to `api.Clock.Now()` in the clock’s location (often UTC), which can select the wrong service date around local midnight and also contradicts the function comment / trips-for-location behavior (which uses `Now().In(currentLocation)`).

## Pull request overview This pull request fixes `stops-for-location`’s `time` query parameter parsing so it correctly accepts the documented formats (epoch millis, `yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss`, and date-only) instead of silently mis-parsing the string form as a small epoch-millis value. **Changes:** - Replaces the handler’s `fmt.Sscanf`-based time parsing with `utils.ParseTimeParameter` and introduces a helper (`queryTimeForStops`) to resolve the service-date selection time. - Adjusts time resolution to use an agency timezone (matching the approach used in `trips-for-location`) and keeps legacy behavior of serving malformed `time` values (HTTP 200) by falling back to “now”. - Adds a table-driven test covering accepted formats, malformed values, and absent `time`, asserting consistent stop lists across accepted representations. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | internal/restapi/stops_for_location_handler.go | Uses `ParseTimeParameter` via a new helper to resolve the query time used for active-service date selection. | | internal/restapi/stops_for_location_handler_test.go | Adds coverage ensuring documented time formats are accepted and produce consistent stop lists. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Nice catch on the underlying bug — `fmt.Sscanf(timeStr, "%d", &timeMs)` happily
reading `2025` off the front of `2025-06-13_14-00-00` and resolving to 1970 is
exactly the kind of silent wrong-answer that's hard to notice from the outside.

Things I checked and that hold up:

- It routes through `utils.ParseTimeParameter` rather than growing another
  parser, which is what CONTRIBUTING.md's Code Reuse section asks for and what
  trips-for-route, stops-for-route, vehicles-for-agency and trips-for-location
  already do. Epoch-vs-string disambiguation is handled inside that helper, so
  a digit-only string can't be mis-read as a date.
- Dropping the 15-minute binning is safe — `queryTime` fed exactly one consumer,
  `.Format("20060102")`, so binning to a quarter hour never affected anything.
- The second commit is the one I'd have asked for if it weren't here: a service
  date is a local calendar date, so taking the fallback in the agency's zone
  rather than the server clock's is correct, and it brings this in line with
  trips-for-location.
- `TestStopsForLocationUsesAgencyDateForCurrentTime` is the good test — two
  instants that are the same local Friday but straddle UTC midnight will fail
  if the fallback ever drifts back to the server zone. That's a real regression
  guard, not a shape check.
- Serving a malformed `time` as 200 rather than 400 preserves legacy behavior,
  and thanks for calling that out in the description rather than leaving me to
  spot it — that's the discrepancy handling CONTRIBUTING.md asks for.

Non-blocking: the comment at the `currentDate` line still reads "for the
requested queryTime", but `queryTime` is the variable this PR deleted. Worth a
one-word fix next time you're in the file.

Merging.
